content: I have a lean 4 axiom free formalization of Robin's 1984 paper on the equivalence of RH and the divisor sum inequality, it includes some small parts from Nicolas' 1983 paper and Landau's oscillation theorem, but it's mixed in with a bunch of other unfinished stuff I'm working on for RH at the moment. Is there any interest in a standalone module of that result, or a reorganization of it that isolates more reusable analytic helper theorems for mathlib? Also wondering what best practice is for organizing modules for papers like this in general, I have some partial work done for Green-Tao 2004 on arithmetic progressions primes and Maynard's 2012 paper on the difference between consecutive primes and would like to finish the whole papers in a way that's useful.

We're all still working this out! You can make formalized material more useful by:

  • taking the time and effort (and gaining the expertise) required to PR it to Mathlib
  • getting it into Tau Ceti, by helping write roadmaps to ensure that the your material is in scope, and then direct an AI to do that actual PRs (and to contribute commensurately to review there)
  • make sure your repositories are registered at https://palomar-registry.org/
    • and in particular have a #formalization.yaml
    • and use #comparator
  • get together with other interested people to build a library downstream of mathlib that gathers together the reusable material in a subfield of mathematics (this can be faster and more flexible than PRing to mathlib)

To be honest "standalone" repositories that don't do at least one of the above may not have much durable value at all!

I haven't looked into Tau Ceti yet, should still do that. I have the repo set up with formalization.yaml and comparator which is passing in CI, but I haven't been able to successfully register on Palomar yet because of a bug, the work is done on lean/mathlib 4.33.1 which it rejects because mathlib master is on 4.34.2-rc and it treats 4.33.1 as not being an ancestor of master. I have a thread up in Palomar channel and have made a PR to the registry repo to accept official release tags, not just the latest ancestors of master.

I have had it go through the repo and separate out what could be reusable for mathlib, but think I'll need to look at Tau Ceti to understand if it's actually in scope or what other work it could separate out for mathlib. The Robin repo is small enough for me to manually check over that work to make sure it fits mathlib, but I have another repo up for Bombieri-Vinagradov which is almost finished with the Siegel-Walfisz part and it's obviously a substantially larger body of theorems.
